parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin pāpa (“pope”), from Koine Greek πάπας (pápas); originally a babble word. Doublet of поп (pop, “priest”).
Borrowed from Late Latin rabbi, and from Koine Greek ῥαββί (rhabbí), from (post-biblical) Hebrew רַבִּי (rabbi, “my master”), from רַב (rav, “master [of]”) + ־י (-i, “me”).

Borrowed in 18th century (no later than 1782) from some Western European derivative of Late Latin Saracenus, from Koine Greek Σαρακηνός (Sarakēnós), further origin uncertain (see there). From New Latin encyclopaedia (“general education”), from a univerbated form of Koine Greek ἐγκύκλιος παιδείᾱ (enkúklios paideíā, “education in the circle of arts and sciences”), from ἐγκύκλιος (enkúklios, “circular”) + παιδείᾱ (paideíā, “child-rearing, education”).
